predecessors.note: Hand-over, not a founding: the Lombards dossier (480-586) already carries the kingdom in Italy from the migration of 568; the 586/587 cut is Cliopatria's change of row (Lombards to Kingdom of Italy).

land.text: Lombardy, Piedmont, Veneto, Friuli, Emilia and Tuscany: the part of the 774 shape that Cliopatria's Kingdom of the Franks shape of 775 covers (525 of 772 cells)

successors.note: 'Charlemagne ... added "and of the Lombards" to his title' (Desiderius page); Pavia fell in June 774 (footnote).

land.text: the Duchy of Spoleto, a Cliopatria row again from 775 (73 cells, all inside the 774 shape)

successors.note: The pages opened are silent on Spoleto's status in 774.

land.text: the Duchy of Benevento, a Cliopatria row again from 775 (167 cells, all inside the 774 shape)

successors.note: The pages opened are silent on Benevento's status in 774.

land.text: the 5 cells of Cliopatria's Papal States shape of 775 that lie inside the 774 shape

successors.note: Roman lands the papacy had received from the kingdom between 728 (Sutri) and 756; Cliopatria's Papal States shape is separate from the kingdom's throughout.

capitals.name: Pavia
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Cividale del Friuli (568-572) Pavia (572-774)'. Fell to Charlemagne in June 774 after an eight-month siege (Desiderius page).

rulers.name: Grimoald
rulers.note: Accession year not on the page; placed at the 661 division of the kingdom between Perctarit and Godepert; death 671 is the page's.

rulers.name: Perctarit
rulers.note: Returned after 671; first, shared reign of 661 (with Godepert, who was killed) has no years on the page.

rulers.name: Liutpert
rulers.note: Drowned; the page's dates for his fall conflict slightly.

rulers.name: Ratchis
rulers.note: Years from the Liutprand page (death 744) and the Aistulf page ('replaced by Aistulf in 749'); the Kingdom page gives none.

rulers.name: Aistulf
rulers.note: Died in December 756 after a hunting accident (Aistulf page).

rulers.name: Desiderius
rulers.note: Infobox 756-774; the Aistulf page has him replacing Aistulf in March 757.

keyframe_review.note: 147,918 km2 (Piedmont, Lombardy, Veneto, Friuli, Tuscany, Umbria, Marche, Abruzzo, Molise, Campania, Basilicata and part of Apulia), 587-601. Infobox area: page silent, so no comparison. The shape draws the duchies of Spoleto and Benevento (the lands south of Tuscany) as direct kingdom, although Cliopatria gives both their own rows in 577-586; the page calls them Langobardia Minor, 'considerably more autonomous' than the northern duchies, so the ledger tints them as vassals (vassal_start 587, confidence 1). The kingdom's capital is Pavia (572-774).

155,199 km2, 602-627: +32 cells in Veneto, Emilia and Lombardy. The page: 'the decade up to 603' saw Lombard advances including Parma, Piacenza, Padua, Monselice, Este, Cremona and Mantua (individual years page silent). The shape starts a year before the page's 603.

157,009 km2, 628-632: +8 cells in Campania and Calabria. Page silent on any Lombard gain there in the 620s (the page lists only Adaloald's deposition in 625 and Arioald 626-636): shape unverified, kept as drawn (unverified: page budget).
157,653 km2, 633-637: +1 cell in Friuli. Page silent; kept as drawn (unverified: page budget).
157,745 km2, 638-640: +1 cell. Page silent; kept as drawn (unverified: page budget).

169,067 km2, 641-643: +42 cells (Emilia 14 to 43, Liguria 1 to 7, Veneto, Tuscany). Rothari page: 'Rothari conquered Genoa in 641' and took Oderzo in 641. The Emilia part runs ahead of the page: the Scultenna battle near Modena, where the exarch's army was beaten, is dated 645. The Exarchate page has Liguria 'completely lost in 640', the Kingdom page 643.

171,790 km2, 644-660: Liguria 7 to 16 cells and Tuscany +2: the rest of Byzantine Liguria. Kingdom page: Rothari's 'conquest of Liguria, including Genoa, Luni and Oderzo' in 643 (the Rothari page: 'the rest of Eastern Roman Liguria in 643'); the shape is a year late. It overlaps Cliopatria's Byzantine Empire shape by 11 cells.

172,091 km2, 661-691 (+0.3k). The page records the division of the kingdom in 661 between Perctarit and Godepert and the battles of Refrancore (663) and Coronate (689), none with a territorial result. Kept as drawn.

179,820 km2, 692-704: +20 cells in Apulia (28 to 48) and 4 in Campania and Basilicata, bbox east to 17.67 E. Page silent on the date; it says 'southern Apulia' was among regions never under Lombard domination, which the eastern Apulian cells (Taranto-Brindisi side) may contradict: a gap-filler should check the Benevento pages. Kept as drawn (unverified: page budget).

correction.text: the shape unchanged, but for 705-726 only; from 727 the 732 shape applies (years change only)

keyframe_review.note: 179,636 km2, 705-731, valid only to 726. Liutprand page: 'In 727, he crossed the Po and took Bologna, Osimo, Rimini and Ancona', with other Emilian cities and the Pentapolis; Cliopatria draws the larger 732 shape five years later.

correction.text: the shape unchanged, but for 727-740 (years change only)

keyframe_review.note: 209,623 km2 (793 cells): Emilia 72, Tuscany 79, Marche 34, Umbria 21, Veneto 61 cells. Valid from 727, not 732: Liutprand page 'In 727, he crossed the Po and took Bologna, Osimo, Rimini and Ancona'; he 'took Classis, the seaport of Ravenna, but could not take Ravenna itself'; Hildeprand held Ravenna briefly in 732 (Kingdom page) and the Venetians expelled the Lombards. The shape holds 3 of the 7 Ravenna-province cells and 7 of the 11 Ferrara cells. Valid to 740.

149,426 km2, 741-749: north Italy, Emilia and Tuscany only: the southern duchies, the Pentapolis (Marche 34 to 2 cells) and part of Umbria and Lazio are out. Liutprand page: Zachary 'signed a twenty-year peace' in 741 and the pope promised 'not to align with the dukes of Spoleto or Benevento', which implies that the dukes stood apart from the king; Zachary 're-acquired four towns' (undated). The shape keeps Ferrara (11 of 11 cells) and 5 of 7 Ravenna cells, more of the Exarchate than the 732 and 750 shapes, which only the 'mid-730s' occupation of Ravenna (Liutprand page) could explain. The exits are Cliopatria's reading; the page is silent on a revolt of the dukes in 739-742, so the ledger records them at confidence 1.

209,095 km2, 750 only: the southern duchies return. Aistulf page: 'In the late spring or summer 751, Aistulf placed Spoleto under his direct control without naming a replacement duke'; the shape is a year early. Aistulf reigned 749-756 (infobox).

218,642 km2, 751-754: Ravenna, Ferrara and the Exarchate. Exarchate page: 'The exarchate fell in 751 with the Lombard conquest of Ravenna at the hands of the Lombard king Aistulf' (the Aistulf page says 750); 'In 752 ... the Ducatus Pentapolis' was conquered by Aistulf (one year after the shape's start).

219,714 km2, 755-756, the kingdom's largest: Lazio 18 to 24 cells; 7 cells overlap Cliopatria's Byzantine Empire shape. Aistulf page: Pepin 'besieged Pavia in 755', the treaty returned Roman lands, 'the Lombard kingdom remained more or less intact'; Aistulf 'besieged Rome again in 756'. The extra Lazio cells have no dated cause on the pages.

210,706 km2, 757-762: -34 cells (Emilia 83 to 67, Marche 36 to 24), the Papal States shape growing by the same amount. Exarchate page: Pepin 'donated the conquered lands back to the Papacy' and 'the separation of the Papal States in 756'; Kingdom page: Ravenna 'went to the pope'. The shape is a year after the page's 756, and the Ravenna (7 to 3 cells) and Ferrara (11 to 7) cells leave in two steps, 757 and 763. Desiderius, king from 756 (March 757 on the Aistulf page), deposed Alboin of Spoleto in 757 and ruled Spoleto himself (Desiderius page).

205,037 km2, 763-774: Emilia 67 to 50 cells and Veneto 59 to 54, the Papal States shape growing to 105 cells. Desiderius page: 'Sometime in 760, envoys from Pepin convinced Desiderius to return some of the cities' he had taken, 'but he did not keep his promises'. The page gives no 763 event; the ledger records the loss at confidence 1.

region.text: the Lombard kingdom in Italy as Cliopatria draws it from 587

ledger.note: 587: the Lombard kingdom of King Authari continues under Cliopatria's new row (a hand-over from the Lombards dossier, not a founding). The page gives 'Autari: 584-590' and the capital Pavia (572-774); it dates nothing at 587.

region.text: the lands of the Duchy of Spoleto (Cliopatria row of 741-749)

ledger.note: 587: the duchies of Spoleto and Benevento are drawn as the kingdom's autonomous south. 'Langobardia Minor': both 'were considerably more autonomous' than the northern duchies (page, undated); Grimoald (died 671) appointed the dukes of Spoleto and Friuli, and in 671 Romuald of Benevento 'pledged loyalty in exchange for recognition of Benevento's autonomy'. Cliopatria folds both into the kingdom's shape from 587; the start year is Cliopatria's, the page is silent.

region.text: the lands of the Duchy of Benevento (Cliopatria row of 741-749)

ledger.note: 587: the Duchy of Benevento as the kingdom's autonomous south (see the Spoleto entry). Under Rothari (636-652) 'Arechi I of Benevento recognized the king's authority' (page, undated within the reign).

region.text: Parma, Piacenza, Padua, Monselice, Este, Cremona and Mantua

ledger.note: c. 603: the Lombards take Padua, Cremona, Mantua and the Po towns from the Exarchate. 'the decade up to 603' saw advances including Parma, Piacenza, Padua, Monselice, Este, Cremona and Mantua; the individual years are not on the page. Cliopatria's shape grows in 602.

region.text: the cells Cliopatria adds in 628

ledger.note: 628: a small southern or Friulian extension (+8 cells in Campania and Calabria). The page is silent: Cliopatria's shape step only, bridged at confidence 1.

region.text: the cells Cliopatria adds in 633

ledger.note: 633: a small southern or Friulian extension (+1 cell in Friuli). The page is silent: Cliopatria's shape step only, bridged at confidence 1.

region.text: the cells Cliopatria adds in 638

ledger.note: 638: a small southern or Friulian extension (+1 cell). The page is silent: Cliopatria's shape step only, bridged at confidence 1.

region.text: Genoa and Oderzo

ledger.note: 641: Rothari conquers Genoa and Oderzo. 'Rothari conquered Genoa in 641' and the Byzantine places 'including Oderzo (Opitergium) in 641'. The Exarchate page has Liguria 'completely lost in 640', the Kingdom page 643.

region.text: Liguria, including Genoa and Luni

ledger.note: 643: Rothari completes the conquest of Liguria. 'Conquest of Liguria, including Genoa, Luni and Oderzo' under Rothari (643); the Rothari page has 'the rest of Eastern Roman Liguria in 643'.

region.text: Modena and the Scultenna valley, Emilia

ledger.note: 645: Rothari beats the exarch on the Scultenna. The exarch's army 'was defeated by Rothari on the banks of the Scultenna' near Modena 'with the loss of 8,000 men, in 645', leaving the empire 'with only the Ravennan marshes in northern Italy'. Cliopatria's Emilia is already in the 641 shape.

region.text: Bologna, Osimo, Rimini and Ancona with the Emilian cities and the Pentapolis

ledger.note: 727: Liutprand crosses the Po. 'In 727, he crossed the Po and took Bologna, Osimo, Rimini and Ancona', other Emilian cities and the Pentapolis, which 'spontaneously' went over. Cliopatria draws the result from 732.

region.text: Classe and Ravenna

ledger.note: 727: the war for Ravenna begins. Liutprand 'took Classis, the seaport of Ravenna, but could not take Ravenna itself'; Hildeprand held the city briefly in 732 (Kingdom page), Liutprand 'again more certainly occupied Ravenna' for a brief period in the mid-730s, and the Venetians expelled the Lombards. The Exarchate page dates the exarch's revolt over iconoclasm to 727.

region.text: Sutri

ledger.note: 728: Liutprand gives Sutri to the papacy. He 'gave Sutri over to the Papacy in 728, all the while maintaining control of the nearby district' (a place-sized donation, below one map cell).

region.text: the lands of the Duchy of Spoleto (Cliopatria row of 741-749)

ledger.note: 741: Spoleto leaves the kingdom's shape. Zachary's twenty-year peace of 741 required 'not to align with the dukes of Spoleto or Benevento'; the page is silent on a revolt in 739-742. Cliopatria gives Spoleto its own row for 741-749.

region.text: the lands of the Duchy of Benevento (Cliopatria row of 741-749)

ledger.note: 741: Benevento leaves the kingdom's shape (see the Spoleto entry); Cliopatria's Benevento row runs 741-749.

region.text: the Marche, Umbria and Lazio cells of the 732 shape that the 741 shape lacks

ledger.note: 741: the Pentapolis and part of Umbria and Lazio fall out of the shape. Page: Zachary 'signed a twenty-year peace' in 741 and 're-acquired four towns' (undated); Cliopatria's Marche drops from 34 to 2 cells.

region.text: the lands of the Duchy of Spoleto (Cliopatria row of 741-749)

ledger.note: 751: Aistulf takes Spoleto into his own hand. 'In the late spring or summer 751, Aistulf placed Spoleto under his direct control without naming a replacement duke'. Cliopatria's shape returns in 750.

region.text: the lands of the Duchy of Benevento (Cliopatria row of 741-749)

ledger.note: 751: Benevento is again within the kingdom's reach. Aistulf 'imposed power on Spoleto and indirectly on Benevento' (page, undated); Cliopatria's shape includes it from 750.

region.text: Ravenna and the provinces of the Exarchate: Ferrara, Comacchio and the land south of Ravenna as far as Perugia

ledger.note: 751: Aistulf takes Ravenna and the Exarchate. 'The exarchate fell in 751 with the Lombard conquest of Ravenna at the hands of the Lombard king Aistulf'; Eutychius, the last exarch, 'was killed by the Lombards in 751'. The Aistulf page has 'In 750, Aistulf captured Ravenna and all the provinces subject to the Exarchate'; the Kingdom page has Istria, Ferrara, Comacchio and the land south of Ravenna to Perugia occupied 'from 750 to 751'.

region.text: Classe and Ravenna

ledger.note: 751: the Exarchate falls and the Lombard-Byzantine fight for Ravenna ends.

region.text: the Ducatus Pentapolis

ledger.note: 752: Aistulf conquers the Pentapolis. 'In 752, the northeastern portion of the Exarchate known as the Ducatus Pentapolis' was 'conquered by King Aistulf of the Lombards'.

region.text: the cells Cliopatria adds in 755 (Lazio 18 to 24)

ledger.note: 755: the shape reaches further into Lazio (18 to 24 cells). Aistulf 'demanded tribute from the Roman duchy itself' (undated) and 'besieged Rome again in 756'; no page dates the cells.

region.text: Pavia, the capital

ledger.note: 755: Pepin besieges Pavia. 'In the spring of 755, the newly anointed Pepin crossed the Alps' and 'besieged Pavia in 755'; he had left Francia in the summer of 754 at Pope Stephen II's call.

region.text: Pavia, the capital

ledger.note: 756: the second Frankish campaign. 'Pepin returned in 756, defeated Aistulf a second time and imposed an annual tribute'; Aistulf died in December 756.

region.text: Ravenna and the Pentapolis, the conquered lands

ledger.note: 756: Pepin's gift. Pepin 'donated the conquered lands back to the Papacy' and 'the separation of the Papal States' followed 'in 756'; the Kingdom page: Ravenna 'went to the pope'. Cliopatria draws the loss from 757.

region.text: the cells of the 757 shape that the 763 shape lacks (Emilia, Veneto)

ledger.note: 763: more Emilia passes to the papacy. 'Sometime in 760, envoys from Pepin convinced Desiderius to return some of the cities' (he did not keep his promises); Cliopatria's shape shrinks in 763 (Emilia 67 to 50 cells; the Ravenna and Ferrara cells go to 0).

region.text: the kingdom, besieged

ledger.note: 773: Charlemagne marches on Pavia. 'During the spring of 773, Charlemagne sent two Frankish armies against the Lombards'; the siege of Pavia lasted eight months.

region.text: the kingdom

ledger.note: 774: Pavia falls. Pavia was captured after an eight-month siege and Desiderius deposed; 'Adelchis and Desiderius co-ruled the region until they were deposed in June 774' (footnote).

region.text: the lands of the Duchy of Benevento (Cliopatria row of 741-749)

ledger.note: 774: Benevento no longer the kingdom's: Cliopatria gives it its own row from 775. The pages are silent on its status in 774.

region.text: the whole kingdom

ledger.note: June 774: Charlemagne takes the Lombard crown. Pavia was captured, Desiderius was exiled to Corbie, and Charlemagne added 'and of the Lombards' to his title while the Lombards kept their laws.

wars.name: Lombard-Frankish wars of the 580s and 590s
wars.outcome: The page lists 'Frankish wars (585, 588, 590s)' and says Authari 'drove the Franks into Piedmont' in 585; the results of 588 and the 590s are not given and Cliopatria's shape does not change in 587-601.
wars.note: Years of the 590s are the page's range; kept as 585-590.

wars.name: Agilulf's advances against the Exarchate

zones.text: Parma, Piacenza, Padua, Monselice, Este, Cremona and Mantua

wars.outcome: Lombard gains in the Po valley 'in the decade up to 603'.
wars.note: The range 593-603 is the page's 'decade up to 603'; no individual year is dated.

wars.name: Rothari's conquest of Byzantine Liguria and Emilia
wars.outcome: Genoa and Oderzo in 641, the rest of Liguria in 643, the exarch's defeat on the Scultenna in 645; Byzantium left with 'only the Ravennan marshes in northern Italy'.

wars.name: Lombard conquest of the Exarchate of Ravenna
wars.outcome: Liutprand's 727 conquests and brief hold on Ravenna in the 730s; Aistulf takes Ravenna in 751 and the Pentapolis in 752, ending the exarchate.
wars.note: Spans two kings; the pages do not describe continuous fighting.

wars.name: Pepin the Short's Italian campaigns against Aistulf

zones.text: the Exarchate lands returned to the pope

wars.outcome: Pepin crossed the Alps in 754 and 755, besieged Pavia in 755 and returned in 756; Aistulf paid an annual tribute and lost the Exarchate lands to the papacy.

wars.name: Desiderius' war on the papacy
wars.outcome: In 772 Adrian I demanded the surrender of territory and Desiderius 'resumed war against Romagna's cities'; in 773 Pope Hadrian 'openly broke with king Desiderius' and called in Charlemagne.
wars.note: The Desiderius page is silent on a war in 771-772.

wars.name: Frankish conquest of the Lombard kingdom (siege of Pavia)
wars.outcome: Charlemagne's two armies of spring 773 besieged Pavia for eight months; it fell in June 774 and the kingdom passed to Charlemagne as 'king of the Lombards'.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is on the pages for the kingdom's frontier with the Exarchate, Venice, the Franks or the Bavarians; the lines of 756 (Pepin's return of the Exarchate to the pope) are described by city, not by line.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 by the Phase B agent for batch eu-13-b. This dossier is the Lombard half of the split of Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of Italy' row (587..1946, 48 shapes): the row joins three states, the Lombard kingdom (shapes 587-774, reviewed here), the medieval Kingdom of Italy (kingdom-of-italy-medieval, 855-961) and the Savoyard Kingdom of Italy (kingdom-of-italy, 1861-1946). The slug kingdom-of-italy stays with the 1861-1946 state, which is the one Cliopatria's Wikidata id (Q172579) and Wikipedia title ('Kingdom of Italy') name.
Pages: six of the nine allowed for 17 shapes (Kingdom of the Lombards, Exarchate of Ravenna, Liutprand, Aistulf, Rothari, Desiderius). The Kingdom page's infobox gives no area, so no area comparison could be made.
Not settled: (1) the 628, 633, 638, 661 and 692 shapes and the 755 Lazio cells have no dated cause on any page (confidence 1 events or 'ok' with the note); the 692 Apulia extension may contradict the Kingdom page's 'southern Apulia never under Lombard domination'. (2) Spoleto and Benevento: Cliopatria draws them as direct kingdom 587-740 and 750-774 but as rows of their own in 577-586, 741-749 and from 775; the vassal entries (587, 741, 751, 774) are the researcher's reading of 'Langobardia Minor ... considerably more autonomous' and are all confidence 1 or 2; the duchy dossiers (duchy-of-spoleto, duchy-of-benevento, written by other parts of eu-13) should carry the matching vassal events. (3) Dates differ between pages: Ravenna 750 (Aistulf page), 751 (Exarchate page), 'from 750 to 751' (Kingdom page); Liguria 640 (Exarchate), 641 (Rothari) and 643 (Kingdom); Desiderius reigns 756 (infobox) or from March 757 (Aistulf page). (4) Hildeprand and Ratchis have no reign years on the pages; Hildeprand is omitted from the ruler strip. (5) The Exarchate of Ravenna, the Duchy of Rome and the Duchy of Friuli are not Cliopatria rows; gains from the Exarchate name the Byzantine rows (eastern-roman-empire to 632, byzantine-empire from 633).
Slug change for neighbours: other dossiers use the counterpart 'kingdom-of-italy' for this state (byzantine-empire ledger and wars, lombards successor); they should now read kingdom-of-the-lombards for 587-774.
Place names the gazetteer may lack: Oderzo, Sutri (given as coordinates), Pavia as a place (the province 'Pavia' is used).
Page budget: six pages for this state; nine pages in all for the three split states are in the sibling dossiers' sources.
